# MCP tools

Every tool `ganymede mcp` and `ganymede serve --mcp` offer an agent,
with its parameters, as the agent's `tools/list` shows them. [Agents over
MCP](mcp.md) has setup, and how the tools fit together. With
`--read-only` or `--no-execute`, the tools that would edit or run stay
listed and refuse ([Options](mcp.md#options)).

<!-- mcp-tools:start (generated by crates/ganymede-server/src/mcp/reference.rs) -->

## `cell_add`

Add a cell without running it: Markdown narration (the default), or with `mode: recorded` a step that ran outside the kernel. With `answers` set to a request cell's id, it goes below that request and marks it done. Returns the new cell's id.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` (required) | string | The cell's source: Markdown, or the command or step it records. |
| `cell_type` | `markdown`, `code`, `raw` | Default markdown. |
| `mode` | `note` (Narration), `recorded` (A step that ran outside the kernel (a shell command, a file the agent wrote), recorded so the notebook tells the whole story) | Default note. |
| `after` | string | Insert after this cell id (default: at the end). |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |
| `mark` | string | A read mark (from an `@@read` line) to move past the new cell, as if its reader had added it: for a hook adding a cell on an agent's behalf, so the agent isn't told of it as someone else's. |
| `answers` | string | The id of a request cell this cell answers: the cell goes after it (unless `after` says otherwise), and the request is marked done, so it is no longer reported as a request. |

## `cell_clear_outputs`

Leave a code cell's outputs out of the notebook: clears them now and whenever the cell runs again through these tools. For output too large or too private to keep; outputs are the record of the run, so keep them otherwise. `keep: true` undoes it for the next run.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | string | The code cell's id. |
| `keep` | boolean | `true` keeps the cell's outputs again from its next run. |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `cell_delete`

Delete a cell. Refused when someone else changed the cell since your last read; read their change in with notebook_read(since), then redo it.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | string | The cell's id. |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `cell_edit`

Replace a cell's source; with `run: true`, run it after. The replaced source is kept in the cell's metadata.ganymede.agent.history; to remove a secret, delete the cell instead. Refused when someone else changed the cell since your last read; read their change in with notebook_read(since), then redo it.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | string | The cell's id. |
| `source` (required) | string | The new source, in place of the whole cell's. |
| `run` | boolean | Run the cell after editing it (code cells). |
| `timeout` | integer | With `run`: seconds to wait for the result (default 600). The cell keeps running after a timeout. |
| `keep_outputs` | boolean | With `run`: keep the outputs in the notebook (default: as the cell had it). `false` leaves them out, as `cell_run`'s `keep_outputs`. |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `cell_move`

Move a cell after another one, or to the top. Refused when someone else changed the cell since your last read; read their change in with notebook_read(since), then redo it.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | string | The id of the cell to move. |
| `after` | string | Put the cell after this one; at the top when left out. |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `cell_run`

Run code in the notebook's kernel and return its outputs. By default the code is recorded as a new code cell (at the end, or after `after`); `record: false` runs it as scratch work that leaves nothing in the notebook and doesn't advance the execution count; it shares the kernel's state, so variables it assigns stay defined.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` (required) | string | Code to run. |
| `after` | string | Insert after this cell id (default: at the end). |
| `record` | boolean | Record the run as a cell (default true). `false` is a scratch run: it runs in the kernel and leaves nothing in the notebook, but its variables stay defined in the kernel. |
| `timeout` | integer | Seconds to wait for the result (default 600). A recorded cell keeps running after a timeout; a scratch run is interrupted. |
| `keep_outputs` | boolean | Keep the outputs in the notebook (default true). `false` records the code but leaves its outputs out of the notebook, now and when it runs again: for output too large or too private to keep. You still get the outputs back. |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `cell_snapshot`

Snapshot cells as Markdown to show the user: the code in a fenced block, each chart or image saved as a PNG (or its own format) file and linked by path, tables (table outputs and HTML tables) as Markdown tables, other output as text. The images also come back to you as images, whatever the server's image setting, so use this to look at a chart before describing it. Runs nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` (required) | array of string | Cell ids, in the order to show them. |
| `dir` | string | Save images in this directory, relative to this connection's directory, such as `journal/snapshots`, for a report next to the notebook. By default they go to a directory outside the server root that only you can read. |
| `code` | boolean | Include each code cell's source (default true). |
| `max_rows` | integer | Rows to keep of a table (default 20). |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `kernel_control`

Interrupt, restart or shut down the notebook's kernel.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` (required) | `interrupt`, `restart`, `shutdown` | What to do to the notebook's kernel. |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `kernelspecs_list`

List the kernels that can run notebooks here, the server's default, and the default for a folder when a `.ganymede.toml` there or above sets one (`kernel = "<name>"`). New notebooks in that folder start it unless `notebook_open` names a kernel.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | The folder to report a default for, relative to this connection's directory (default: that directory). |

## `notebook_open`

Open a notebook, creating it if it doesn't exist, and start or join its kernel. Later calls may leave out `path`. Paths are relative to the directory the reply names: the server's root, or your own folder when `ganymede mcp` forwards to a server rooted above it, where a leading / starts at the root. Returns a compact view of the notebook.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` (required) | string | Notebook path, such as `analysis/run.ipynb`, relative to this connection's directory (`notebook_open` names it); a leading `/` starts at the server root. |
| `kernel` | string | Kernelspec name for a new notebook or a new kernel (default: the notebook's own, else its folder's default from `.ganymede.toml`, else the server's default). |
| `title` | string | For a new notebook: a title, written as a first Markdown cell. |

## `notebook_publish`

Publish the notebook as one self-contained HTML page to read and share: title, contents, Markdown as prose, charts and tables inline, code folded under each result, light and dark. The page holds only the notebook's cells and outputs (no metadata), makes no network requests and runs no notebook script; the server root, home directory and token (8 characters or more) are replaced wherever they appear as a whole name. Unless `code` is `hidden` or `download` is false, the page also carries a copy of the notebook with a Download notebook button, with the same replacements and without metadata or recorded parameters. Saves it under the server root, at `out` relative to this connection's directory (default `published/<name>.html` beside the notebook), replacing an earlier published page but no other file unless `overwrite: true`, and returns its path. Runs nothing; run the notebook first so the outputs are current.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `out` | string | Where to save the page, relative to this connection's directory, ending in `.html`. Default: `published/<name>.html` beside the notebook. |
| `code` | string | How code shows: `folded` under each result (default), `shown`, or `hidden`. |
| `byline` | string | A line under the title. Default: today's date. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | Replace `out` even when it isn't an earlier published page. |
| `download` | boolean | Put a copy of the notebook in the page, with a Download notebook button: redacted as the page is, without metadata or recorded parameters. Default: on, unless `code` is `hidden`. |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `notebook_read`

Read a notebook as text: cells with their ids, sources and outputs, then an `@@read <mark>` line. With `since: <mark>`, return only the cells others (a person, another agent) added, edited, deleted, moved or ran since the read that gave the mark; your own edits and runs through these tools are left out.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |
| `since` | string | A read mark from an earlier read's `@@read` line: return only the cells others added, edited, deleted, moved or ran since that read. Without `path`, the mark's notebook. The mark becomes this connection's for that notebook, so its own edits move it. |

## `notebook_requests`

List the requests to you that are still open: Markdown cells starting `@agent` (or `@` and your client's name) that a person wrote in a notebook open in this server, through JupyterLab or the apps, and that no cell answers yet. Answer one with cell_add, `answers` set to its id.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; every notebook open in the server when left out. |

## `notebook_run_all`

Run every code cell in order, after restarting the kernel unless `restart: false`, and return the notebook.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `restart` | boolean | Restart the kernel first (default true). |
| `timeout` | integer | Seconds to wait for every cell to finish (default 600). Cells keep running after a timeout. |
| `path` | string | Notebook path; the one last opened when left out. |

## `notebooks_list`

List notebooks and directories in a directory.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | Directory relative to this connection's directory (default: that directory); a leading `/` starts at the server root. |

## `notebooks_search`

Search notebooks under a directory (default: this connection's directory, with subdirectories) for cells containing every word of `query`, ignoring case. Searches sources, and text outputs with `outputs: true`. Returns each matching cell's notebook, title, index, id, type and an excerpt; read a hit in full with `notebook_read`. Use it before starting a journal, to find what earlier notebooks found.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` (required) | string | Words to find, all of them, in any case and order. |
| `dir` | string | Directory to search, with its subdirectories, relative to this connection's directory (default: that directory); a leading `/` starts at the server root. |
| `outputs` | boolean | Search text outputs too, not only sources (default false). |
| `cell_type` | string | Only cells of this type: `code`, `markdown` or `raw`. |
| `limit` | integer | Most matching cells to return (default 20, at most 200). |
